name: ForestDB
tagline: Couchbase's HB+-trie key-value storage library; no longer actively developed.
description: ForestDB is an embeddable key-value storage library from Couchbase whose main index is an HB+-trie: a trie of small B+-trees keyed on fixed-size chunks of the key, which keeps lookups shallow even for long keys. It combines an append-only file with a write-ahead log and an in-memory WAL index, and offers MVCC snapshots, rollback to an earlier commit, iteration by key or sequence number and per-file compaction. The design was published in IEEE Transactions on Computers and reached v1.2 in June 2016. Couchbase now states in its commits that ForestDB is not under active development; it is still compiled as part of the Couchbase Server build, so only build fixes land. Use it to study the HB+-trie, not for new systems.
statusNote: Couchbase says ForestDB is no longer under active development; it receives only build fixes (latest 2024) because it is still part of the Couchbase Server build.

scale.notes: Single-process library; distribution is left to the embedding system.

strengths: HB+-trie keeps index depth low for long, variable-length keys
MVCC snapshots and rollback to a previous commit point
Iterate by key range or by sequence number
Peer-reviewed design with a public benchmark harness
weaknesses: No feature development; Couchbase only keeps it compiling
Transactions offer read-committed or read-uncommitted isolation only
Append-only files need compaction tuning to control space amplification
Small ecosystem: no maintained bindings beyond C/C++
useCases: Maintaining software that already embeds ForestDB
Benchmark comparisons against LSM and B-tree engines
